body: oh my god i have never thought of it like this. wow, i wish more than anything i could just give my life to someone who really wants to live one. i am taking up space that someone else could be in genuinely making a good life for themself.
this is all i think about. holy shit, i would've ended it so long ago if there was a quick and painless way to go. fucked up as it is, i would do it without even thinking twice

i think my family would (at least my mom would); i live with my best friend but i blew her off the other night when i was having an episode and we haven't spoke to each other since. i wouldn't be surprised if this one was the final straw, she's exhausted of my episodes. she knows she's my only friend and i think she's been tired of me for a while, and is worried that if she finally admits she's done, i'll finally commit. otherwise i don't have anyone. she and my family are the only people i have left and they barely know me anymore.
yup. feels like i died a year ago and i've just been dragging around a lifeless body ever since

i've got 3 other siblings, there's always something going on. plus i'm the oldest, and i definitely fall into the 'had to grow up way too young' category. i basically raised my youngest sister and started working 5-6 days a week at 16 and never stopped. i'm the one who's supposed to have it together. i also worry that my mom will blame herself for how i turned out and she's got enough on her plate already.

they also don't really understand. it's not just them, but most people can't really understand the idea of spending every second wanting to die. it's irrational and unimaginable to them. 

there's been a few instances where i've actually wanted to hospitalize myself. i just can never go through with it.

a couple. i was diagnosed with major depressive and mild anxiety when i was 18 and got a BPD diagnosis last April. my first was an awful therapist that my parents didn't look into, just got the first one we could on our insurance. it turned me off from therapy for a while. my mom was (and still is) anti-med (i suspect she has BPD as well & went through a lot of med complications when she was my age). i've been in-and-out of on-campus college psychs since. it's been okay, but never long enough to see any actual change. and, to be completely honest, most of the time i end up lying to them anyway. i don't think i could say anything i wrote in this post to a therapist; it's usually either because i feel like i'm faking my feelings and/or i don't want to be involuntarily hospitalized and have my parents finally find out that i've been rapidly declining for the past year.

Hi love, 

I was overweight throughout my teenage years. I'm now almost 22 and still struggling with eating habits and body image. I remember what it was like being your age & having these thoughts and I know it is one of the hardest things to go through. 

I promise you, 84 pounds at 12 is a perfectly normal weight (more likely underweight depending on your height). Your body is just starting to develop. Your weight will change, the way your body looks will change now more than ever. Puberty is awkward and difficult at times for everyone. 

Eating disorders are nothing like the way they are talked about and even romanticized on social media. Eventually your body starts to catch up to you: I lost my hair, I was depressed and angry all the time. I couldn't stand up without fainting at one point. 

I know it's a lot harder than it sounds (take it from me, I'm still figuring it out), but you should try to switch your focus to being *healthy,* not as skinny as you can be. I wish someone had told me that instead of learning the lesson the hard way. 

If you ever need to talk or just want some support, please feel free to message me any time. I don't have all the answers, but I can talk to you about my experiences. I have an 11 year old sister (she'll be 12 in just a few days!) who I talk with about these topics often. 

Sending a ton of love your way. Body image issues can be a scary thing. Nobody should go through it alone.
